Given below are few statements with reference to the major events in the menstrual cycle of a human female :
(i) During the follicular phase, the primary follicles grow to become a Graafian follicle.
(ii) Gonadotropins FSH and progesterone stimulate follicular development during the follicular phase.
(iii) LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle thereby releasing the corpus luteum.
(iv) Progesterone released by corpus luteum is essential for maintenance of endometrium.
(v) Both LH and progesterone attain a peak level in the middle of the cycle.
Choose the option with all true statements from the given options :
questions._cbseVoided: Award 1 mark if the child has attempted any one option.
questions._flag: KEYLESS VOID: the scheme prints no letter, only 'Award 1 mark if the child has attempted any one option.' No option is correct: only (i) and (iv) are true ((ii) the gonadotropins are FSH and LH, not progesterone; (iii) the LH surge releases the ovum, not the corpus luteum; (v) LH peaks mid-cycle but progesterone peaks in the luteal phase), and no option is exactly (i) and (iv).

Study the pedigree chart of a family showing the inheritance of myotonic dystrophy :
The trait under study is :
questions._figure: REQUIRED: a three-generation pedigree. Generation I is a mated couple (a female circle and a male square); generation II is their four children, left to right a daughter, a son, a son married to an outside female and a daughter married to an outside male; generation III is the first married couple's three children (two daughters and a son) and the second couple's three children (a son, a daughter and a son). Which symbols are shaded (affected) decides the mode of inheritance, so the shading is withheld here. Page idx 6.
questions._flag: The shading pattern alone does not exclude a dominant X-linked trait (no affected male has children, so the father-to-daughter test cannot be applied); the key (C) rests on myotonic dystrophy being the autosomal dominant disorder NCERT names. Official key kept.

Given below are the diagrammatic representations of the replicating fork of DNA in E. coli. Study the diagrams and answer the questions that follow.
(a) Which one of the three diagrams (i), (ii) or (iii) is the correct representation of the replicating fork of DNA replication ? Explain your answer.
(b) Name the enzyme used in E. coli to join the newly synthesised fragments of DNA.
questions._figure: REQUIRED: three Y-shaped replication forks labelled (i), (ii) and (iii), each with base-pair rungs on the unwound stem and arrows along the two new strands in the arms. The parental strand ends are labelled: (i) 3' and 5' at the top, 5' and 3' at the foot of the arms; (ii) 5' and 3' at the top, 3' and 5' at the foot; (iii) 3' and 5' at the top, 5' and 3' at the foot. Which way each arrow points and which arm carries a single long arrow or short broken ones IS the answer to (a), so it is withheld here. Page idx 12.

questions.stem:
The basic scheme of the essential steps involved in the process of recombinant DNA technology is summarised below in the form of a flow diagram. Study the given flow diagram and answer the questions that follow :
Step-1 Plasmid DNA (cut using Restriction Enzyme EcoR I) + Foreign DNA (cut using Restriction Enzyme EcoR I)
\(\downarrow\) DNA ligase
Step-2 Recombinant DNA molecule
\(\downarrow\)
Step-3 Transfer of recombinant DNA molecule to the host cell
\(\downarrow\)
Step-4 Replication of recombinant DNA molecule in the host cell
(a) Name the specific enzyme that might have been used to make the multiple copies of foreign DNA before undergoing Step-1 of the process.
(b) How does the use of restriction enzyme EcoR I in Step-1 facilitate the action of DNA ligase to form the recombinant DNA molecule ? Explain.
(c) Name the most commonly used host in the above process.

questions.context:
Highly conserved proteins such as Haemoglobin and Cytochrome-C provide the best biochemical evidences to trace evolutionary relationships between different groups. Cytochrome-C is formed of 104 amino acids. Cytochrome-C is the respiratory pigment present in all eukaryotic cells. It has evolved at a constant rate during evolution. In chimpanzees and humans, Cytochrome-C genes are identical. The given data shows the evolution of the Cytochrome-C gene in different mammals from kangaroos, cows, rodents to humans :
| Groups | Nucleotide substitution in the gene of Cytochrome-C | Millions of years ago |
|---|---|---|
| Human/Kangaroo | 100 | 125 mya |
| Human/Cow | 75 | 120 mya |
| Human/Rodent | 60 | 75 mya |

questions.context: In 2021, \(5{\cdot}3\) percent of 15 to 16-year-olds worldwide (\(13{\cdot}5\) million individuals) had used Cannabis in the past year according to UNODC. The adolescent brain is still developing and drug use can have long-term negative effects. Early drug use initiation can lead to faster development of dependence than in adults and other problems in adulthood. Parts of the Amazon Basin are at the intersection of multiple forms of organised crimes that are accelerating devastation, with severe implications for the security, health and well-being of the population across the region. The direct impact of coca cultivation on deforestation is minimal, but indirectly it acts as a catalyst for "Narco-deforestation". The laundering of drug trafficking profits into land speculation etc. is posing a growing danger to the world's largest rainforest.
